title: Epic D: Packed TN storage and capability
description:
Rollup epic for changing local Translation Notes storage from tens of thousands of raw markdown files to a packed per-book JSON representation, with a dedicated TN capability.

Background:
Translation Notes are read-only reference resources. Treating them as huge trees of standalone markdown files is expensive to import, expensive to index, and expensive to read at runtime. Preserving the generic document API for TN would force packed storage to impersonate the old file-level shape and keep complexity in consumers.

Technical approach:
Define a TN-specific capability, reshape imported TN content into one packed JSON file per book, and teach loaders plus TN UI flows to use the packed capability directly rather than the generic document seam.

Project value:
This dramatically reduces local file counts, makes imports disk-friendlier, simplifies caching, and provides a better foundation for future read-only resource types.
acceptance_criteria: Epic is complete when TN imports produce per-book packed files, packed TN resources load successfully through the resource system, and TN UI consumers read via the new capability rather than generic document enumeration.
notes: This epic intentionally breaks from the newly-added generic TN document path; do not preserve that path for compatibility if it complicates the packed storage design. Keep the packed format identical across web and desktop.

title: Document the import/loader/typed-item architecture in an ADR
description:
Write an ADR or architecture note that captures the clarified import, loader, and typed-item architecture in repo terms.

## Background
This refactor has already diverged once because the boundary language was not locked early enough. A fresh implementer needs one repo-local source of truth that states: import chooses storage strategy, loaders return typed loaded items, UI branches by type, and capabilities drive affordances.

The repo already contains an accepted March 23 `BaseResource / Project` ADR at `product-docs/specs/base-resource-project-architecture.md`. This documentation bead must explicitly supersede that ADR rather than preserve both models in parallel. The output should make the older ADR historical, not co-governing.

## Technical Approach
- Write a concise ADR or architecture note in `product-docs/specs/` or the most appropriate architecture-doc location.
- Document the four layers: managed files, import, loader, app/library UI.
- Define the meaning of `type`, `containerFormat`, and capabilities in repo terms.
- Include concrete examples for `usfmScripture` and `translationNotes`.
- Point readers to the core contracts and the major service/UI seams they affect.
- Explicitly state that this ADR supersedes `product-docs/specs/base-resource-project-architecture.md`, and either replace that document or mark it historical/superseded.

## Success Criteria
- A future implementer can understand the target architecture without rereading planning context.
- The relationship to the existing `BaseResource / Project` ADR is explicit and unambiguous.
- Code terminology, bead terminology, and architecture documentation match.
- There is no ambiguity about which ADR governs future work in this area.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The repo has one explicit architecture source of truth for this refactor.
- The March 23 `BaseResource / Project` ADR is marked superseded or replaced.
- The new ADR matches the final contract terminology used in code and beads.
- Readers cannot reasonably interpret both ADRs as co-equal current guidance.

## Test Plan

- Manual verification that cited repo touchpoints still match the ADR after implementation.

title: Refactor reference panel flows to branch once by item type
description:
Refactor the reference-panel hooks and components so they branch once by type and then use type-specific contracts.

## Background
The reference panel is the clearest proof point for the typed-item model: scripture and TN are both readable, but they are not the same app-facing shape. The UI should perform one higher-level switch on `type`, then render and query through the appropriate type-specific contract.

For TN specifically, this bead should reflect the live `@ai` guidance in `src/app/domain/reference/translationNotes.ts`: the UI should render stored raw markdown content with a markdown renderer such as `react-markdown`, not rely on custom heading/body section parsing as an intermediate view model.

## Technical Approach
- Update reference hooks to expose the active item type and the correct type-specific query/runtime surface.
- Keep shared state only where it is genuinely shared: selection, sync toggles, active path, and other panel-level controls.
- Render reference content through one top-level switch by type.
- Render TN from raw markdown content using a markdown renderer rather than a custom parsed-section transform.
- Preserve current read-only scripture behavior and TN rendering behavior unless a separate bead changes UX intentionally.

## Repo Touchpoints

- `src/app/ui/components/blocks/ReferenceEditor.tsx`

## Success Criteria
- The reference panel no longer relies on a broad abstraction that mixes scripture and TN internals.
- Scripture and TN rendering paths are clearly separated behind a single type switch.
- TN rendering is based on raw markdown input rather than custom section parsing.
- Existing reference UX remains behaviorally stable while internal branching becomes clearer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reference hooks expose the active item type and type-specific runtime/query surface.
- Rendering branches once by type.
- TN rendering consumes raw markdown content through a markdown renderer.

## Test Plan

title: Epic A: Establish BaseResource core model and architecture contract
description:
## Background
This epic introduces the new architecture boundary for local content in Dovetail. The goal is to separate a generic, read-only `BaseResource` abstraction from the scripture-specific writable `Project` model.

The base seam must not be Bible-shaped. It must support at least:
- scripture USFM resources that can later be promoted into editable projects
- Translation Notes style anchorable resources
- grouped document collections such as Translation Words (`kt/*`, `names/*`, `other/*`)

## Scope
This epic covers the core contracts and architectural documentation needed before loader and UI work can safely proceed.

## Why This Exists
The current system collapses all loaded resources into scripture editing concepts. That blocks clean support for read-only reference resources and risks turning `Project` into a mushy do-everything type. This epic defines the new seam so later work can stay disciplined.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria
- Core work under this epic results in a generic `BaseResource` model that does not assume books, chapters, verses, writability, or git.
- `Project` remains explicitly scripture-specific and writable.
- The resulting contracts are detailed enough that downstream beads do not need to reinterpret the architecture.
notes:
Test plan
- Unit tests for any normalization helpers introduced under this epic.
- Type-level or runtime guard tests for capability detection.

Delegation notes
- This epic itself is a parent container. Child beads carry the actual implementation work.
- Complexity label should guide assignment of child beads; this epic should not be executed directly.

title: Define BaseResource core contracts and normalized descriptor
description:

## Technical Approach
- Introduce a normalized `BaseResourceDescriptor` with stable id, display name, resource kind, container format, language, and read-only state.
- Introduce a `BaseResource` interface that exposes document listing and document read by stable opaque document id.
- Support optional browse/group path metadata for grouped resources without forcing a full tree contract.
- Explicitly avoid scripture assumptions such as `bookCode`, chapters, verses, canonical order, or writability.

## Considerations
This bead must make it obvious that generic addressing is document-oriented. Grouping paths such as `kt/faith` or `names/abraham` are browse metadata, not evidence that the base model is Bible-shaped.

- The base contract can represent grouped markdown collections without requiring scripture anchors.

title: Define optional capabilities for scripture anchor resolution and remote sync
description:
## Background
The new model needs specialization without turning `BaseResource` into a kitchen-sink interface. This bead introduces narrow capabilities that only some resources implement.

## Technical Approach
- Add a `ScriptureAnchorAddressable` capability for resources that can resolve a scripture anchor into zero or more readable items.
- Add a `RemoteSyncCapable` capability for resources that preserve remote/source metadata and can eventually check/apply updates.
- Keep writability out of capabilities and on scripture-specific `Project`.

## Considerations
`RemoteSyncCapable` should reserve the seam for remote-backed read-only resources. It should be compatible with the policy that shallow clone is the default strategy when cloning such resources, but the policy should not become a type-level hard guarantee.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria
- Capability interfaces or equivalent guards exist for scripture anchor resolution and remote sync.
- Anchor resolution is optional and not part of the base contract.
- Remote sync/update shape is optional and not part of the base contract.
- Writability remains separate from generic and optional capabilities.

title: Epic E: Remote read-only update model
description:
Rollup epic for remote-source metadata and update behavior on packed read-only TN resources.

Background:
Once TN resources are packed into a disk-friendly local representation, the app can no longer treat the active local files as a plain clone that supports git pull. Updates need to be modeled explicitly as fetch/reimport/repack.

Technical approach:
Preserve remote origin metadata on packed resources and implement update behavior as full replacement of the local packed payload, followed by reindexing. Do not attempt incremental patching or merge semantics in this wave.

Project value:
This keeps remote read-only resources maintainable after the storage-format shift without pretending packed local files are a writable clone.
acceptance_criteria: Epic is complete when packed TN resources preserve enough metadata for update checks and the update flow replaces and repacks the resource locally instead of relying on git pull semantics.
notes: Update semantics must be identical in meaning across web and desktop, even if the transport/materialization path differs by platform.

title: Route remote web imports through the shared import service and progress model
description:
Unify the remote web import path under the shared import service and progress model.

Background:
Remote imports should look identical to local imports from the create flow perspective: same progress semantics, same project/resource distinction, and no special-case UI behavior.

Technical approach:
Wrap the existing remote materialization flow in the shared import adapter, map its download/materialization phases into the standardized progress contract, and preserve downstream inspect/reshape/index behavior.

Implementation requirements:
- Remote web imports must report phase-based progress.
- Final result handling must remain identical to local imports.
- This bead must not decide packed TN update semantics; it only covers initial remote import on web.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria:
- Remote web imports are routed through the import service.
- Shared progress and result semantics are preserved.
- Unit coverage pins remote import status mapping.

- Regression tests for success/failure messaging.

Implementation requirements:

- Remote-source metadata support should remain attachable downstream.

- The TN capability is available to consumers.

title: Implement the first TN adapter and reference-panel renderer
description:
## Background
Translation Notes is the first non-scripture proving case for the new architecture. This bead must show that a read-only, anchorable resource can load and render in the real reference panel.

## Technical Approach
- Implement a TN resource adapter for nested markdown by book/chapter/verse.
- Build a lightweight scripture-anchor index over TN items.
- Resolve active scripture anchors to zero or more TN items.
- Load note bodies lazily with nearby prefetch to keep sequential navigation responsive.
- Render TN content in the reference panel through a dedicated renderer chosen by resource kind/capability.
- Show an explicit empty state when no TN content exists for the active anchor.

## Considerations
The core resource contract should remain document-oriented. Any indexing structure here is adapter-specific, not a new base-resource requirement.

Success criteria
- A TN resource can be selected in the reference panel and render note content for the active scripture anchor.
- The TN path uses a real loadable fixture or equivalent end-to-end resource shape, not only the existing content-only sample directory.
- Missing anchor content shows a clear empty state.
- Lazy loading and nearby prefetch do not break sequential navigation behavior.
- The implementation proves the architecture without turning TN into a fake scripture project.

Background:

title: Cloud publishing and reconciliation for editable scripture projects
description:
## Background
Add cloud publishing and reconciliation for editable scripture projects only. This feature sits on top of Dovetail's existing local-first editing model: explicit Review & Save, local Git-backed history, and scripture compare flows. The goal is not generic remote sync. The goal is a non-technical user experience for connecting a Gitea account, linking or creating a remote repo, saving locally first, publishing after save, and explicitly reviewing incoming scripture changes when the remote has advanced.

The reviewed design artifacts for this scope are:
- product-docs/ideas/2026-03-27-cloud-publishing-state-review.html
- product-docs/ideas/2026-03-27-cloud-publishing-pseudocode.md

This epic exists so the implementation DAG can stay self-contained even if later agents never open those documents.

## Product North Star
- Product framing is cloud publishing and reconciliation.
- Scope is editable scripture projects only in v1.
- Web and Tauri both ship through shared domain contracts.
- Local save remains authoritative and must succeed first.
- USFM differences are always surfaced explicitly through Dovetail review; no silent merge behavior.
- No user-facing merge-commit or rebase vocabulary.
- Web must not visibly behave worse than Tauri.

## Architectural Story
The feature breaks down into a small number of major concerns:
1. Durable remote linkage facts that live with a project.
2. Mutable per-project remote status that is app-local, not tracked in Git.
3. App-global auth/session behavior.
4. Git transport/history plumbing that preserves branch shape without merge commits.
5. Compare/review entry that treats remote latest as another compare source.
6. Save/publish orchestration that keeps local-first semantics intact.
7. UI and settings behavior that expose the feature without leaking raw Git concepts.
8. Export/share sanitization and validation so linkage is not accidentally portable.

## Expected Outcome
After the child beads land, a user should be able to:
- connect a Gitea account
- create or link a remote repo for an editable scripture project
- save locally and auto-publish if enabled
- explicitly sync when desired
- review incoming remote scripture changes in the same general family of Dovetail review UI
- reopen on another browser or machine and pull work back in
- stay safe when offline, when behind, or when local unpublished commits exist

## Test Philosophy
Every child bead must explicitly include test work. The implementation should follow the testing pyramid:
- unit tests for state classification, settings guards, link parsing, and metadata rewrite logic
- integration tests for orchestration boundaries and remote classification/publish behavior
- e2e coverage for the highest-value user flows only

## Coordination Note
The child beads form the implementation plan. They should be dependency-complete enough that an agent can start from any ready child and understand why it exists, what seams it touches, what it must not break, and how it will be verified.

title: Define remote vocabulary, durable link file, and per-project status ownership
description:
## Background
This bead establishes the foundational vocabulary and state ownership rules for cloud publishing. The repo currently has a local Git seam and separate reference-resource remote affordances, but it does not yet have a durable, scripture-project-specific remote linkage model. Without a clear vocabulary and persisted shape, every later bead risks inventing slightly different meanings for link state, session state, and per-project cloud status.

## Scope
Create the shared type and persistence foundation for:
- durable project-local remote linkage facts
- per-project app-local mutable remote status
- app-global auth/session state
- settings flags that guard auto-sync-on-open and auto-push-on-save

This is the bead that tells the story of what belongs in the project versus what belongs only on the current machine.

## Technical Approach
- Extend `src/app/data/settings.ts` with explicit remote-networking policy fields.
- Add shared `remote` or `gitRemote` types in a central location that can be imported by app/core/web/tauri code.
- Add a dedicated Dovetail-owned project file helper for durable remote info, currently envisioned as `projectLocalGitRemoteInfo.ts`.
- Define the durable remote-info filename string once and only once through a shared constant; downstream code should import that constant rather than restating the filename.
- Add a per-project app-local status persistence helper keyed by project path.
- Make the storage split explicit:
  - project-local durable remote info file inside the project
  - app-local per-project status in a new app-data-style storage location reached through the FS service / storage roots abstraction
  - app-local install-global session state in the same app-data-style storage family, but isolated from per-project status records
- If the current `StorageRoots` contract does not yet have an appropriate app-data location, this bead should introduce one explicitly rather than hiding these files in ad hoc paths.
- Keep the naming split intentional: product copy can stay “cloud”, while implementation names can use `remote` / `gitRemote` for precision.

## Canonical Status Set
The canonical per-project remote status values introduced by this bead should be explicitly enumerated and shared by later beads:
- `connected`
- `syncing`
- `offline`
- `pendingPublish`
- `remoteUpdatesAvailable`
- `needsReview`
- `reauthRequired`

The bead should also define which timestamps and head references are part of the canonical status record, such as `lastCheckedAt`, `lastPublishedAt`, `lastKnownLocalHead`, and `lastKnownRemoteHead`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Durable linkage facts have one canonical type and one canonical read/write boundary.
- Mutable per-project status has one canonical type and one canonical storage boundary.
- Settings contract includes explicit auto-sync and auto-push flags.
- The bead documents and enforces that `pendingPublish`, `needsReview`, `offline`, and `lastChecked` belong to the project conceptually but remain app-local in persistence.
- The canonical remote status enum/list is defined once and reused later.
- The app-local persistence path for status/session uses a clear storage-root-backed abstraction instead of ad hoc local paths.
- The durable remote-info filename is defined exactly once through a shared constant.
- No remote transport work is required yet; this bead is about shape, names, and persistence boundaries.

## Test Plan
- Unit: link-file parse/write/read validation, including absent-file behavior.
- Unit: per-project status store CRUD and keyed persistence behavior.
- Unit: canonical status value validation and serialization behavior.
- Unit: settings defaults and read/write behavior for new networking flags.
- Unit: schema/version rejection behavior if the project-local remote info file changes later.
- Integration: storage-root-backed status/session persistence resolves to the intended app-data location on both platforms.

## Considerations
- This bead should make later implementation cheaper by removing naming churn.
- Export/share paths depend on this bead because they must know exactly what file to strip.
- Agents implementing later beads should not have to guess whether a piece of state is project-local, app-local, or session-global.
close_reason: Implemented shared remote state roots, types, settings, and persistence helpers with tests

title: Add app-global auth session management and remote networking settings
description:
## Background
Cloud publishing requires two app-global behaviors that do not belong inside the project: auth/session state and user policy about when network crossings happen automatically. The reviewed design calls out a small session machine plus a settings-driven policy machine. This bead implements the persistence and service seams for those two machines.

## Scope
- Introduce the shared auth/session contract (`AuthSessionProvider` or equivalent final name).
- Persist exactly one active session per install.
- Model best-effort token revocation on logout with bounded retry.
- Wire settings so auto-sync-on-open and auto-push-on-save are explicit guards, not ad hoc booleans inside save/open code.
- Make the provider target explicit: this scope is for Gitea OAuth bearer-token session management, not a generic future provider abstraction.

## Technical Approach
- Add the shared session types and provider interface under the remote/gitRemote domain.
- Add web and tauri adapter stubs or basic implementations for session persistence and access.
- Persist session state in app-local storage reached through the same FS/storage-root-backed app-data strategy introduced by the foundation bead, not in any project path.
- Add logout bookkeeping for token ID and retry count so failed remote deletion can be retried a bounded number of times.
- Use Gitea OAuth bearer tokens as the session/auth substrate for API and repo operations that later beads will need.
- Extend existing settings manager adapters and defaults so the new flags are available on both platforms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exactly one session can be loaded, replaced, and cleared per install.
- Logout clears local session immediately even if remote deletion fails.
- Revocation retries stop after terminal failures or retry-limit exhaustion.
- Settings expose the two remote-network policy flags on both web and tauri.
- The bead explicitly models Gitea OAuth bearer-token session behavior rather than a generic placeholder auth provider.
- Session persistence uses the agreed app-data-style storage boundary rather than an unrelated project path.
- Later beads can consume auth/session and settings through stable interfaces without knowing storage details.

## Test Plan
- Unit: session persistence and reload behavior.
- Unit: logout state transitions, including retryable and terminal revocation outcomes.
- Unit: token-id retry bookkeeping and retry limit behavior.
- Unit: settings defaults and mutation behavior for new flags.
- Integration: platform adapters expose the same setting/session semantics even if the underlying persistence differs.
- Integration: session files/records land under the agreed app-data storage boundary.

## Considerations
- Keep auth/session out of `GitProvider`; session is API/auth state, not repository state.
- This bead should not yet implement full repo listing or publish behavior; it is the policy/auth substrate for those flows.
close_reason: Implemented app-global auth session provider, bounded revocation bookkeeping, and bootstrap wiring

title: Implement remote repo discovery, creation, linking, and writable clone flows
description:
## Background
The primary happy path is: local editable project -> create remote -> link -> publish. The feature also needs a “from my cloud projects” source for bringing writable cloud repos back into the app. This bead owns the service-level project/repo orchestration before save/review semantics kick in.

## Scope
- Repo listing for writable repos, including topic filtering and pagination.
- Programmatic remote repo creation for local projects.
- Linking an existing local editable project to a remote repo.
- Cloning a writable remote repo into a new local editable project while preserving Git history.
- Validation and indexing behavior around the clone/import path.

## Technical Approach
- Extend `DefaultProjectsService` or adjacent orchestration layers to support repo-list, repo-create, attach, and clone flows.
- Implement a `GitRemoteProjectService`-style orchestration seam that composes `GitProvider` plus auth/catalog APIs, rather than re-owning low-level Git transport internally.
- Use the remote service seam for repo catalog and link creation, but reuse current project open/import/index patterns where possible.
- Preserve Git history only on the writable linked-clone path.
- Fail fast on unsupported or invalid remote repo contents instead of silently importing a linked editable project that the app cannot actually support.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A linked project can be created from an existing local project without shell commands.
- A writable cloud repo can be cloned into a new editable local project with its Git history preserved.
- Repo listing supports server-side paging and topic filtering.
- Invalid repo structure fails import instead of silently degrading into a broken linked project.
- Durable project-local remote info is written exactly once a link/clone succeeds.
- The orchestration seam clearly composes `GitProvider` with auth/catalog APIs instead of duplicating Git plumbing.

## Test Plan
- Unit: repo list filtering and paging result mapping.
- Integration: create remote + attach local project writes correct durable link data.
- Integration: clone linked remote preserves history and indexes/open succeeds.
- Integration: invalid remote repo shape fails at the boundary.
- Integration: orchestration calls low-level Git plumbing through `GitProvider` rather than bypassing it.

## Considerations
- This bead is intentionally upstream of save/publish and compare/review concerns.
- It should keep current import/open architecture intact rather than creating a second project-loading path.

title: Extend GitProvider with remote inspection, publish, and replay plumbing
description:
## Background
The most fragile part of this feature is not the UI; it is the branch/history model underneath. The product requires no user-visible merge commits, no user-visible rebase vocabulary, and explicit scripture review. But Git still cares about graph shape. This bead owns the low-level repository plumbing so later orchestration can classify remote state, publish safely, and preserve local unpublished commits.

## Scope
- Extend `GitProvider` to own as much actual Git fetch/push/replay plumbing as practical.
- Add remote state inspection (`upToDate`, `aheadOnly`, `behindOnly`, `diverged`, `untrackedRemote`).
- Add lightweight head inspection separate from heavy content fetch.
- Add hidden replay/rebase-on-top-of-remote behavior for unpublished local commits.
- Keep the result non-merge-commit and non-squash from the user’s perspective.

## Technical Approach
- Add shared Git-level methods needed by web and tauri adapters for fetch, publish, inspect, and replay.
- Keep `GitRemoteProjectService` as a higher-level orchestration seam that composes this plumbing rather than replacing it.
- Separate `inspect remote state` from `fetch full remote contents` so open-time checks stay cheap.
- Codify two key rules:
  1. Remote advanced + only dirty in memory: resolve against `remoteLatest`, then commit directly on top of `remoteLatest`.
  2. Remote advanced + unpublished local commits: replay those local commits onto `remoteLatest` under the hood before final save/publish.
- Surface replay failures as higher-level status transitions, not raw Git errors in the normal UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Git adapters expose shared remote inspection and publish/replay behavior on both web and tauri.
- The low-level API can distinguish head-only inspection from heavier snapshot fetch.
- Reconciliation with unpublished local commits preserves commit history without merge commits or squash fallback.
- Later orchestration beads can ask Git for relationship classification without reimplementing graph logic.
- Service-layer orchestration can compose these capabilities cleanly instead of owning duplicate transport logic.

## Test Plan
- Unit: relationship classification for local/remote head combinations.
- Unit: replay path selection based on dirty-memory-only versus unpublished-local-commit scenarios.
- Integration: publish success, offline failure, remote-advanced rejection.
- Integration: hidden replay path keeps local commits in history on top of remote latest.
- Platform regression: web and tauri adapters conform to the same contract behavior.

## Considerations
- This bead is a blocker for reliable publish and reliable review-after-divergence.
- It should keep auth/session concerns out of Git plumbing while still accepting credentials from the auth layer.
- The implementing agent should verify web-specific auth behavior against the chosen Git transport library rather than assuming parity with Tauri.

title: Implement open-time remote status hydration and background sync classification
description:
## Background
Once a project is linked, opening the project should remain fast and local-first, but the app also needs to know whether remote state has changed. This bead models the background open-time cloud check and status hydration path. It should not block the editor shell, but it should leave the project in a truthful, inspectable state.

## Scope
- Read durable project-local remote info on open.
- Hydrate per-project remote status for the current install.
- Run the open-time background remote check when settings allow it.
- Classify `connected`, `offline`, `remoteUpdatesAvailable`, `needsReview`, and `reauthRequired` transitions.

## Technical Approach
- Extend `projectToParsed.tsx` or adjacent open orchestration to read remote info after local Git readiness but before or during workspace hydration.
- Use the settings/auth/session seams as guards.
- Use lightweight remote-state inspection first; only fetch heavier content later if review is actually needed.
- Leave UI opening non-blocking even when the network check runs.
- Keep the classification logic isolated enough that later UI beads consume a stable status result instead of reproducing open-time decision trees.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A linked project can open locally even when offline or when the remote check is slow.
- Open-time remote checking respects the auto-sync-on-open setting.
- Missing/expired session marks `reauthRequired` instead of pretending the project is healthy.
- Remote differences update the per-project status store in a way later UI can render.
- Status classification rules are explicit enough that later beads do not need to rediscover the state machine.

## Test Plan
- Unit: status classification from combinations of settings/session/local-head/remote-head results.
- Unit: guard evaluation for auto-sync-on-open enabled vs disabled.
- Integration: linked project open with auto-sync enabled updates status in the background.
- Integration: linked project open with auto-sync disabled does not perform remote inspection automatically.
- Integration: offline/missing session/remote-advanced scenarios classify correctly.
- E2E: open linked project and observe non-blocking status update behavior.

## Considerations
- This bead should not own the compare UI entry itself; it only prepares status and deferred action context.
- It depends on durable remote info, session/settings seams, and low-level remote-state inspection.

title: Add remote-latest compare source and reuse compare/review orchestration
description:
## Background
Dovetail already has a left/right compare seam and a diff/review family of UI for scripture changes. This feature should reuse that seam rather than inventing a second reconciliation system. The important design boundary is that `useExternalCompare` remains the compare orchestrator for that branch, while remote latest becomes one additional compare source.

## Scope
- Add a remote-latest compare source kind and loading path.
- Convert fetched remote scripture state into the current compare-source model.
- Let explicit sync or `needsReview` enter the same general review family as existing compare flows.
- Keep resolved content in working memory until explicit `Review & Save`.

## Technical Approach
- Extend compare source types to represent remote latest.
- Add a builder/bridge that takes remote snapshot data plus metadata rules and produces the source shape that compare already expects.
- Keep `useExternalCompare` focused on compare orchestration and apply semantics.
- Reuse the current left/right review modal family rather than inventing a second remote-review modal.
- Enter that modal intentionally from explicit sync actions or banner/status actions; do not auto-populate or auto-open the review modal as a side effect of a background sync finishing.
- Keep the compare-source builder small and testable so transport-layer fetch logic and compare-layer shape logic do not get tangled together.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Remote latest can be loaded as a compare source without introducing a second review stack.
- Remote incoming scripture changes are labeled clearly as incoming cloud/remote changes.
- Applying remote hunks/chapters updates working memory only; it does not silently create commits.
- The compare path remains compatible with existing previous-version and external-project behavior.
- The compare-source builder has a clear, reusable contract for later orchestration beads.
- Remote review uses the current modal family intentionally rather than appearing automatically from background sync completion.

## Test Plan
- Unit: compare source builder for remote latest.
- Unit: remote snapshot normalization into compare-compatible scripture shape.
- Integration: explicit sync enters compare flow with remote latest as the right side.
- Integration: banner/action entry opens the existing modal family with the remote compare source loaded.
- Integration: background sync completion updates status without auto-opening the review modal.
- Regression: existing compare-source kinds still work after adding remote latest.

## Considerations
- This bead should not own publish behavior; it prepares and executes review/apply semantics only.
- Bulk actions should still work, but USFM review remains explicit even when Git could merge mechanically.

title: Implement local-save-first publish pipeline and derived metadata rewrite
description:
## Background
The feature succeeds or fails on one invariant: local save first, cloud publish second. This bead owns the path from explicit Review & Save through derived metadata rewrite, local commit, publish attempt, and transition into `connected`, `pendingPublish`, or `needsReview`.

## Scope
- Keep `useSaveAndRevert` as the local save anchor.
- Regenerate derived metadata before final save/publish when project format requires it.
- Publish after save when settings allow it.
- Leave local commits in place when publish fails.
- Enter the proper per-project status when offline or when the remote has advanced.

## Technical Approach
- Extend the save path with a post-commit publish coordinator guarded by settings and project linkage.
- Rewrite derived metadata such as scripture-burrito checksums before the final write/commit step.
- Treat non-derived manifest fields that change remotely as an explicit TODO/no-op for now; do not invent resolution semantics in this bead beyond preserving current behavior and documenting the gap.
- On publish failure due to remote advancement, preserve the local save commit and set `needsReview`.
- On offline failure, preserve the local save commit and set `pendingPublish`.
- When a replay-on-top-of-remote path is required, use the Git plumbing bead’s capabilities before final publish.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Explicit save still succeeds even when publish cannot happen.
- Derived metadata is regenerated as part of the save/publish boundary, not left stale.
- Non-derived manifest-field conflict handling is left as an explicit documented TODO/no-op rather than guessed silently.
- Publish success, offline failure, and remote-advanced rejection each map to the correct per-project status.
- Local save checkpoints are never discarded just because cloud publication failed.

## Test Plan
- Integration: save + auto-publish success.
- Integration: save + offline -> `pendingPublish`.
- Integration: save + remote advanced -> `needsReview` with local save preserved.
- Unit: metadata rewrite rules for supported project formats.
- Regression: unsupported non-derived manifest-field updates remain unchanged/no-op until a later explicit design decision.
- E2E: linked project save path from dirty working state to local checkpoint and cloud attempt.

## Considerations
- The implementing agent should keep the modal family coherent with current `Review & Save` behavior instead of inventing parallel save affordances.
- This bead is central to the primary user story and should be treated as one of the highest-risk behavior changes.

title: Build account, create/import, status, and explicit sync UI surfaces
description:
## Background
The backend behavior is not enough. Users need understandable surfaces for connecting an account, creating or selecting a remote repo, syncing explicitly, seeing status, and entering review from banners or actions instead of raw Git errors. This bead owns the visible surface area without trying to redesign every editor screen.

## Scope
- Account connection and logout affordances.
- Create/import flow support for “From my cloud projects”.
- Status surfaces for connected/offline/pending-publish/needs-review/reauth-required.
- Explicit sync action.
- Banner or status-trigger entry into the relevant review UI when remote changes are available.

## Technical Approach
- Extend existing create/import route UI rather than inventing a separate cloud dashboard.
- Keep one-button bias where possible for non-technical users, while preserving explicit sync as an action.
- Use status badges/banners rather than modal spam for open-time notifications.
- Keep the UI language non-Git even when the underlying code and Git plumbing are more explicit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A logged-in user can see and choose writable cloud repos from the create/import flow.
- A linked project shows truthful status with user-friendly language.
- The user can explicitly sync even if auto policy flags are disabled.
- Remote-open notifications surface a banner that opens the relevant review UI instead of forcing a modal immediately.

## Test Plan
- Integration: create/import flow shows remote source and list behavior.
- Integration: status rendering maps correctly from per-project status store values.
- E2E: account connect + create remote + save/publish + banner/review entry flow.
- Accessibility/manual verification: banners and status affordances remain discoverable on desktop and smaller layouts.

## Considerations
- This bead should follow, not redefine, the state machines from upstream beads.
- Keep product vocabulary friendly even if code names use `gitRemote` or `remote` internally.

title: Add sanitization, validation, observability, and final docs coverage
description:
## Background
The feature adds new portable and non-portable state, new import/clone boundaries, and new user-visible behavior. Without explicit sanitization, validation, and documentation, the implementation can easily leak remote linkage into exports or allow unsupported remote repos into the editable workflow. This bead closes the loop and makes the system safe to operate.

## Scope
- Strip `.git` and durable remote-info files from export/share/import-zip paths.
- Preserve or reject extra files according to the reviewed policy.
- Validate remote repo contents at clone/open boundaries.
- Add documentation and logging updates needed for future implementers and testers.
- Perform a final cross-cutting verification pass over the feature DAG.

## Technical Approach
- Reuse current export/share/import boundary code where possible.
- Make sanitization deterministic and tested.
- Treat the stripped set explicitly as at least:
  - `.git`
  - the Dovetail durable remote-info file introduced by the foundation bead
- Document the behavior in product/docs/agent-facing docs where the repository currently explains local Git versioning and save behavior.
- Add detailed logs around remote classification, replay path choice, and sanitization decisions so failures are diagnosable during pre-alpha.
- Use this bead as the cross-cutting verification pass for the whole feature, not just as cleanup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shared/exported artifacts do not carry `.git` or the durable remote-info file.
- Unsupported linked remote repo contents fail validation instead of producing a broken local experience.
- The final documentation tells future agents and maintainers how the feature is intended to work without reopening design docs.
- The bead explicitly verifies the end-to-end path of: create/link remote -> save/publish -> reopen on another machine/browser -> sync/review incoming changes -> offline/pending-publish recovery.
- The feature has a final verification pass that covers unit/integration/e2e expectations from the whole scope.

## Test Plan
- Integration: export/share/import strips or preserves the correct files.
- Integration: invalid remote repo contents are rejected with clear errors.
- Regression: local-only import/export behavior is not broken by sanitization logic.
- Integration/E2E verification matrix: create/link -> publish -> reopen -> sync/review -> offline recovery.
- Docs/manual verification: local Git versioning docs and feature docs reflect the new cloud behavior accurately.

## Considerations
- This bead is intentionally late in the DAG because it depends on upstream types, link-file shape, and clone/export boundaries being real.
- Include doc updates rather than treating them as optional cleanup; the feature substantially changes project behavior.

title: Add resource-aware open/list/query plumbing for reference-only resources
description:
## Background
The reference panel needs a broader local resource library than the main Projects page. The graph currently bundles that broader resource-opening/query behavior into the same bead as main workspace route gating, which makes delegation blurry and couples two different concerns.

## Technical Approach
- Add app/service plumbing that can list, query, and open broader `BaseResource` instances for reference-only use.
- Keep this path separate from the scripture-specific `Project` opening path.
- Expose enough information for the reference layer to select resources by kind/type/domain without routing them through the main project workspace.
- Preserve current top-level naming where practical while making the internal service seam resource-aware.

## Considerations
This bead is specifically about the reference-resource open/list path. It is not responsible for main route gating and it is not responsible for UI rendering. Splitting it out should make the app-layer work more fungible and reduce coupling between route safety and reference-resource enablement.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria
- App/services can list and open broader resources for reference-only use without using the main `Project` path.
- Reference-related flows can access resource kind/type/domain metadata needed for downstream selection and rendering.
- The service seam between editable scripture projects and reference-only resources is explicit.
notes:
Implementation notes
## Test plan
- Service tests for listing and opening reference-only resources separately from projects.
- Mixed-library query tests for grouped/type-aware reference-resource results.

## Logging and diagnostics
- Add diagnostics around reference-resource selection/open decisions so it is clear which service path was used.

## Complexity
- Relative complexity: 4/5.

title: Thread remote-backed resource metadata into the optional RemoteSyncCapable seam
description:
## Background
The architecture reserves remote sync for some read-only resources, but the current bead graph only defines the capability contract. It does not yet require the implementation path that preserves remote-backed resource metadata after loading.

## Technical Approach
- Thread remote/source metadata from supported SB/RC-backed resources into the opened resource model without adding git operations to `BaseResource`.
- Materialize the optional `RemoteSyncCapable` seam for resources that have enough source information.
- Preserve the default policy that shallow clone is the preferred implementation strategy for remote-backed read-only resources, while keeping that policy out of the type contract and out of the v1 UI.
- Keep this bead model-only: no end-user update UI, no revert/history semantics for reference-only resources.

## Considerations
This bead exists so remote-backed reference resources do not lose their future update path during the refactor. The system should be able to remember where a resource came from and expose that through an optional capability without pretending the resource is writable or versioned like a project.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria
- Supported resources can preserve source/remote metadata through the load path without polluting `BaseResource`.
- Optional `RemoteSyncCapable` wiring exists for resources with sufficient metadata.
- No user-facing update UI is introduced in v1.
- The implementation preserves the future ability to check/apply updates for reference-only resources.
notes:
Implementation notes
## Test plan
- Unit tests for remote/source metadata extraction and optional capability exposure.
- Regression tests proving resources without remotes do not expose the sync seam.

## Logging and diagnostics
- Add diagnostics around detection of remote-backed resources and whether sync capability wiring was attached.

## Complexity
- Relative complexity: 3/5.

title: Refactor import contracts around storage shaping instead of loading
description:
Refactor the import contracts and orchestration so import is explicitly a storage-shaping phase, not a loader or UI concern.

## Background
The current import flow works, but responsibility is split across app API helpers, service orchestration, importer plumbing, and platform-specific handlers. The clarified model is: import receives folder, zip, or remote input, reads metadata while bytes are still incoming, chooses a storage strategy by app-facing type, writes the managed representation, and returns import result metadata. It should not construct runtime loaded objects.

## Technical Approach
- Preserve the current entrypoints (`importFolder`, `importZip`, `importRemoteZip`) while narrowing their responsibility to managed storage shaping.
- Define the stable import result payload that later layers need: managed path, display/index metadata, type, and any editability/remote hints that belong at import completion time.
- Move loader-like interpretation out of import seams.
- Keep web and desktop implementations conceptually aligned even if their file APIs differ.

## Repo Touchpoints
- `src/app/domain/api/import.tsx`
- `src/core/persistence/ImportService.ts`
- `src/tauri/persistence/TauriImportService.ts`
- `tests/unit/core/persistence/importServiceContracts.test.ts`
- `tests/unit/persistence/TauriImportService.test.ts`

## Success Criteria
- Import code stops constructing or returning app-facing loaded runtime objects.
- Import decisions are finalized before managed storage is considered complete.
- Progress phases still map cleanly to the revised import lifecycle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Import entrypoints are explicitly storage-shaping only.
- Import returns stable metadata instead of runtime loaded objects.
- Web and Tauri import flows share the same conceptual stages.

## Test Plan
- Unit tests for import result shape and progress phases.
- Regression tests for folder, zip, and remote archive entrypoints on both supported platforms.
close_reason: Refactored import contracts around storage shaping. Renamed ImportProjectResult to ImportResult with cleaner structure: item: {id, displayName, managedPath, type} instead of project: ProjectListItem. Import is now explicitly a storage-shaping phase that returns stable metadata, not runtime loaded objects.

title: Epic F: Verification and hardening
description:
Rollup epic for end-to-end verification and regression protection across the new import architecture and packed TN runtime.

Background:
This plan changes import UX, platform boundaries, and the on-disk format for a major reference resource. Verification needs to prove not only that the new flows work, but also that editable scripture imports and non-TN resources remain intact.

Technical approach:
Add focused e2e and integration coverage for long-running TN imports, progress observability, reference rendering, and regression coverage for editable scripture project imports.

Project value:
This reduces the risk of trading performance or architecture gains for regressions in existing user-critical flows.
acceptance_criteria: Epic is complete when there is explicit coverage for TN import/reference usage across platforms and regression coverage for editable project imports plus unaffected non-TN resources.
notes: The test pyramid matters: prefer unit coverage for phase logic and reshape correctness, integration coverage for adapters and loaders, and e2e only for the user-critical workflows.

title: Add a Rust command for native directory copy into managed app storage
description:
Add the Rust command that copies a user-selected source directory into managed app storage on desktop, with structured progress and cleanup.

Background:
The real desktop performance win comes from letting Rust copy files directly from the selected source path instead of streaming them through JS file objects and per-file webview writes.

Technical approach:
Add a Tauri command that accepts a selected source directory and destination metadata, performs recursive copy into managed app storage, emits structured progress events, and cleans up partial destinations on failure. JS should only invoke the command and forward progress into the shared import UI.

Implementation requirements:
- Rust owns recursive copy and partial cleanup.
- Progress events should include counts where feasible.
- Command must integrate with existing managed app storage layout.
- The command should not assume TN-specific packing; it only materializes the raw source directory.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria:
- Desktop folder import no longer marshals file contents through JS writes.
- Rust emits progress for long-running copies.
- Partial failures leave no broken half-imported directory behind.
notes:
Test plan:
- Rust unit/integration tests for recursive copy and cleanup.
- JS integration tests for progress-event handling.

Complexity: 5/5.
close_reason: Implemented and validated with native Rust directory materialization and cleanup

title: Epic B: Web import adapter
description:
Rollup epic for the web implementation of the new import service.

Background:
Web cannot receive durable native filesystem paths, so it must still accept browser-selected files and write them into app-controlled storage. The practical ceiling for performance is bounded-concurrency IO plus minimizing redundant copies and making long-running work observable.

Technical approach:
Implement separate directory, zip, and remote import adapters behind the shared import seam. Directory imports should avoid the extra temp-to-final copy that previously doubled the cost. Zip imports should expose real extract/copy phases instead of one opaque spinner.

Project value:
This preserves a working web path while making it materially faster and less opaque for large read-only resources such as Translation Notes.
acceptance_criteria: Epic is complete when web directory, zip, and remote imports all use the shared import service, avoid unnecessary extra copies, report phase-based progress, and preserve current success/failure behavior for projects versus reference resources.
notes: Do not use unbounded Promise.all on large file sets. Bounded concurrency and phase-level diagnostics are required. Tests should cover cleanup and progress sequencing, not just happy-path completion.

title: Verify, harden, and clean up the typed-item architecture
description:
Epic rollup for verification, cleanup, and migration hardening. This epic ensures the new typed-item model is fully embedded, regression-protected, terminology-consistent, and safe to delegate later without hidden planning context.

## Background
This final wave is not just test hardening. It is the point where the repo should stop carrying the older March 23 `BaseResource / Project` ADR as active architecture for this area. Verification and cleanup under this epic should leave one clear model in place: import shapes managed files, loaders return typed items, UI branches by type, and capabilities determine affordances.

## Success Criteria
- Regression coverage is adequate across all touched seams.
- Transitional naming and adapter cleanup is complete.
- The superseding typed-item architecture is the only active guidance for this area.
- The repo is safe for fresh delegation against the bead set.
close_reason: Verification, cleanup, and migration hardening are complete

title: Introduce a LibraryService-style top-level app seam
close_reason: Introduced LibraryService interface in src/app/services/LibraryService.ts. Defined IndexedLibraryItem type with managedPath, displayName, type, containerFormat, isEditable, hasRemoteSync, languageCode, languageName. Created toIndexedLibraryItem helper function. LibraryService provides listLibraryItems, listCurrentProjects, openItem (returns typed LibraryItem), import methods, and reconcileIndex.

title: Implement scripture and TN runtime loader APIs by type
description:
Implement the type-specific runtime loader APIs for scripture and TN.

## Background
The UI should not consume a fake generic reader. It should receive the runtime contract it actually needs. For scripture that means the current workspace and book-oriented operations used by the editor and read-only scripture flows. For TN that means chapter and book note access over packed book files.

This bead also needs to resolve the live `@ai` note in `src/app/domain/reference/translationNotes.ts`: TN runtime data should stay as raw markdown strings per verse/chapter, not a homegrown section-parsed intermediate format. Rendering concerns belong in the UI layer.

## Technical Approach
- Implement the `usfmScripture` runtime API in terms of the current scripture operations already used by editing and read-only reference flows.
- Implement the `translationNotes` runtime API around packed-book reads and chapter-level access.
- Keep TN runtime output as raw markdown content keyed by verse/chapter rather than pre-parsed heading/body section objects.
- Keep capability attachment separate from these type-specific runtime contracts.
- Ensure read-only scripture in the reference panel can still use the scripture runtime contract without collapsing TN into the same shape.

## Repo Touchpoints
- `src/core/domain/project/ProjectLoader.ts`
- `src/core/domain/project/ResourceContainerProjectLoader.ts`
- `src/core/domain/project/ScriptureBurritoProjectLoader.ts`
- `src/core/persistence/TranslationNotes.ts`
- reference-panel and translation-notes tests under `tests/unit/app`

## Success Criteria
- Scripture consumers call scripture operations directly without TN-specific guards.
- TN consumers call TN operations directly without pretending TN is a generic document list.
- TN runtime data is raw markdown suitable for a markdown renderer rather than custom section parsing.
- The reference panel can branch once by type and use the correct runtime contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scripture runtime operations are available through the `usfmScripture` variant.
- TN runtime operations are available through the `translationNotes` variant.
- TN runtime output preserves raw markdown strings rather than pre-splitting them into synthetic sections.
- Reference flows can use the correct runtime contract after one type switch.

## Test Plan
- Unit tests for TN packed-book chapter reads.
- Regression tests proving TN runtime output remains raw markdown suitable for renderer consumption.
- Regression tests for scripture workspace loading and read-only scripture loading.
- Loader tests covering equivalent behavior for RC and SB resources where appropriate.
close_reason: done

title: Epic C: Desktop native import adapter
description:
Rollup epic for the desktop-native import path.

Background:
Desktop currently routes folder and zip selection through browser file inputs, then pays JS/webview marshalling costs for large file trees. That leaves the desktop path constrained by the same file-object and write-bridge overhead as the web path, which wastes the native capabilities already available in Tauri.

Technical approach:
Replace browser file inputs on desktop with native dialog selection, pass the chosen source paths to Rust commands, and let Rust perform copy/unzip work directly into managed app storage while streaming structured progress back to JS.

Project value:
This is the real performance fix for large desktop imports and also establishes the right architecture for future remote-resource materialization and updates.
acceptance_criteria: Epic is complete when desktop folder and zip imports no longer rely on webview FileList marshalling, Rust handles file materialization into app storage, and progress/events integrate cleanly with the shared app import UI.
notes: Rust commands should own cleanup semantics for partial imports and emit enough progress detail that UI no longer appears frozen on large resources. Keep desktop-specific concerns behind the desktop adapter.

title: Add regression coverage for editable scripture imports and non-TN resources
description:
Add regression coverage for editable scripture imports and unaffected non-TN resources after the import-architecture and packed-TN changes.

Background:
This project cannot trade away editable scripture import behavior or other reference-resource stability while improving TN import and storage. Regression protection needs to prove that non-targeted flows still work.

Technical approach:
Add focused tests for editable scripture directory/zip imports and non-TN read-only resource behavior under the new import service seam. Ensure these flows still classify, open, and message correctly.

Implementation requirements:
- Cover editable scripture imports through the new shared import service.
- Cover at least one non-TN read-only resource path to prove no accidental coupling to TN storage changes.
- Keep tests focused on behavior most likely to regress from adapter and loader changes.

title: Add a Rust command for native zip import into managed app storage
description:

Background:

Implementation requirements:
- Rust owns archive extraction and cleanup.
- Progress events must distinguish extraction from final copy/materialization if those are separate phases.
- JS remains orchestration only.
- Keep compatibility with downstream inspect/reshape/index steps.

title: Implement the web directory import adapter with bounded-concurrency writes
description:
Implement the web directory import adapter behind the shared import service using browser FileList input plus bounded-concurrency writes into app-managed storage.

Background:
Web cannot receive a durable host filesystem path, so directory import must still flow through browser-selected files. The previous implementation paid an unnecessary temp-to-final copy and used serial writes, which is especially punishing for huge resources with many small files.

Technical approach:
Accept the browser folder selection, resolve the final managed destination directory once, write directly into that destination, and use bounded concurrency for file materialization. Emit copy-phase progress using the shared progress model from A3.

Implementation requirements:
- No extra temp-to-final directory copy.
- Use bounded concurrency rather than serial writes or unbounded Promise.all.
- Preserve cleanup behavior if import fails mid-copy.
- Hand off to later inspect/reshape work through the shared import service result flow.
- Make progress counts reflect copied items rather than a frozen spinner.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria:
- Web folder import performs one write pass into managed storage.
- Large imports show live copy progress.
- Partial failures clean up the partially imported directory.
- Unit/integration coverage pins bounded-concurrency behavior and cleanup semantics.
notes:
Test plan:
- Unit tests for progress sequence and direct-to-final write semantics.
- Failure-path tests for partial cleanup.
- Regression tests for existing directory import success behavior.

Complexity: 4/5.
close_reason: Implemented and validated with bounded-concurrency direct-to-final web folder imports

title: Implement the TN reshape pipeline from raw source trees into per-book JSON
description:
Implement the reshape pipeline that converts raw imported TN source trees into packed per-book JSON files.

Background:
The main disk and runtime win comes from collapsing large TN source trees into a much smaller local representation optimized for read-only use. This reshape work must preserve the note content while dramatically reducing file count and future IO calls.

Technical approach:
Read raw TN source content, group entries by book/chapter/verse, serialize one packed JSON file per book, and store that packed payload as the canonical local TN representation. The raw source layout should no longer be the steady-state local read format.

Implementation requirements:
- Preserve markdown note bodies faithfully.
- Produce deterministic packed output from the same source.
- Work for both web and desktop import paths.
- Clean up partial packed output if reshape fails.
- Integrate with progress phases so users can see reshape work during TN imports.

- The `en_tn_condensed` fixture reshapes correctly.
- Failure paths do not leave half-reshaped resources behind.
notes:

- Serialization correctness tests for grouped chapter/verse content.
- Failure cleanup tests.

Define a single app-facing service interface with operations for directory, zip, and remote imports. Define normalized result payloads that distinguish editable projects from read-only resources, and normalized progress payloads that represent phase-based progress instead of UI-specific strings only. Inject this service through app context alongside ProjectsService and other platform services.

Implementation requirements:
- Service contract must be platform-agnostic.
- Result type must preserve current project/resource distinction.
- Progress payloads must support phase-oriented updates and failure diagnostics.
- The contract should be decision-complete enough that web and desktop adapters can be implemented independently afterward.

title: Clarify typed loaded-item core model and capability boundaries
description:
Epic rollup for clarifying the primary app-facing model: files on disk are loaded into typed items, and capabilities hang off those typed items. This epic exists to keep the new vocabulary decision-complete before later implementation beads proceed.

## Background
The current divergence introduced the right move away from scripture-only assumptions, but the model is still muddy because `BaseResource`, `Project`, `resourceKind`, and capability concepts overlap. The target model is: import decides storage strategy, loaders return typed app-facing contracts, UI branches by type, and capabilities determine affordances.

This epic is working from a newer architectural reality than the March 23 `BaseResource / Project` ADR. The implementation graph under this epic should be read as superseding that older two-layer model rather than preserving both worldviews.

## Success Criteria
- The repo has one primary app-facing discriminant, `type`, clearly separated from low-level `containerFormat`.
- `resourceKind` is eliminated or collapsed into the new app-facing model.
- The typed loaded-item and capability model are explicit enough that downstream beads do not need to reinterpret the architecture.
- The older `BaseResource / Project` ADR is no longer treated as governing architecture for this area.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Core type and capability vocabulary is decision-complete.
- Downstream beads can rely on one explicit model without reinterpretation.
- Docs and tests back the final vocabulary.

## Test Plan
- Type-level and unit coverage for the new core contracts.
- Documentation coverage for the intended boundary language.
close_reason: All child beads are closed; rollup epic complete

title: Make metadata-first import branching explicit for scripture and TN
description:
Make metadata-first import branching decision-complete for `usfmScripture` versus `translationNotes`.

## Background
The new architecture depends on import branching once by app-facing type. Scripture should preserve source shape and retain existing editable-project setup behavior. TN should reshape into packed `{book}.json` files while preserving metadata and non-book support files. This decision must be made from metadata while input is still being imported, not after storage is written.

## Technical Approach
- Read container metadata early from folder, zip, and remote import sources.
- Resolve one app-facing `type` from metadata before writing the final managed representation.
- For scripture: preserve current source/workspace shape and existing editable-scripture setup behavior.
- For TN: write packed book files, preserve support/root files, and avoid storing the raw imported TN tree as the final managed shape.
- Preserve remote origin metadata only when the import source is actually remote or user-selected as remote-backed.

## Success Criteria
- Import branches once by app-facing type and does not resniff later in the pipeline.
- Scripture and TN land in the correct managed disk representation for later loading and indexing.
- Non-scripture, non-TN resources are not accidentally packed or rewritten.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Type is resolved from metadata before writing managed storage.
- Scripture import preserves editable scripture shape.
- TN import packs book data and preserves required support files.
- No later pipeline stage needs to resniff type.

title: Introduce typed loader contracts for managed paths
description:
Introduce explicit typed loader contracts so loaders return app-facing variants, not generic partially-capable resources.

The clarified architecture says loader input is a managed path on disk and loader output is a typed app-facing contract. Today the code still routes through generic `openResource` and `openProject` seams with optional methods glued on. This bead establishes the typed loader seam that later UI and service work can rely on.

This work should follow the newer typed-item architecture and migrate away from the older March 23 `BaseResource / Project` ADR. Do not preserve the old generic-BaseResource-first loader worldview as a parallel first-class model.

- Define the loader contract for managed paths with typed-item output.
- Keep the initial loader variants limited to `usfmScripture` and `translationNotes`.

- Loader implementation direction is aligned with the superseding typed-item architecture, not the older `BaseResource / Project` ADR.

- Loader contract is path-in and typed-item-out.
- Consumers branch once on `type` and stop depending on optional ad hoc methods.

title: Define the TN-specific capability and packed per-book TN storage contract
description:

title: Implement full reimport-and-repack updates for remote read-only TN resources
description:
Implement remote TN updates as full reimport-and-repack rather than git pull against packed local files.

Background:
Packed TN storage is optimized for read-only local use, not for acting as a live clone. The correct update model is to fetch/update the source resource, replace the local packed representation, and reindex.

Technical approach:
Build an update flow that materializes the remote resource through the appropriate platform adapter, repacks it into the canonical local TN format, replaces the existing local packed payload, and refreshes indexing.

Implementation requirements:
- Replace-and-repack is the only update model in this wave.
- Preserve remote-source metadata after update.
- Handle failure so an existing good local resource is not destroyed without replacement.
- Keep semantics aligned across web and desktop.
acceptance_criteria:
Success criteria:
- Remote TN updates replace the local packed resource via reimport/repack.
- No part of the system relies on git pull against packed TN files.
- Integration coverage proves replacement semantics and failure handling.
